the criteria for evaluating qualitative research should include the extent to which the researcher's own experience is included in the research, the extent to which that experience is analyzed and theorized, and the extent to which it is relevant to the study's topic.

the lived experiences of individuals and groups.
the ways in which we live in the world.
the lived experience of people in their social worlds (Ellis, & Bochner, 1996).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

autoethnography is a research genre that combines autobiography with ethnography, and it is a methodological tool for the researcher to use to study his/her own experience (Adams, Ellis, & Bochner, 1997) I learned that autoethnographic texts are not written to be judged by the same standards of academic writing.

autoethnography is a qualitative research method that is used by a researcher to study his or her own personal experience and connect this personal experience to wider cultural, social, and/or organizational issues.
autoethnography was not a scholarly genre I had learned to appreciate and practice before.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autoethnography is a form of writing that is personal in nature, but not necessarily personal in content.
autoethnography is a form of qualitative research that focuses on the self in the social world (Ellis, Bochner, Adams & Mattingly, 2011).
autoethnography is a qualitative method of inquiry that involves the researcher's personal experience as data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the politics of autoethnography is to write in the first person and in the present tense.
autoethnography is not an empirical method.
autoethnography was not a method to be used in the study of narrative practice, but a practice of narrative practice.
